podcast-dannyjones-j2GCOfdNE1c:
Former Scientology executive Mike Rinder joins Danny Jones for an episode of the KONCRETE Podcast, numbered 68. The title calls Rinder the top threat to Scientology. Rinder once ran the church's dirty work and now works to expose it.

Rinder tells how the church tracks and fights its foes, and why leaders fear him most. He shares tales from his years at the top and his break for freedom. Jones asks what it would take for the church to fall. Listeners get an insider's map of a secret faith at war with its own past. The library keeps the talk as an archive record.
podcast-joerogan-4YqZ08GxV1c:
Comedian Duncan Trussell visits the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 1464, one of many stops in a long friendship between the two hosts. Trussell mixes stand-up humor with a real interest in psychedelics and Eastern thought. His episodes rarely stay on one subject for long.

The talk drifts from drug trips and the nature of the self to death, love, and the jokes hidden inside all three. Rogan plays the grounded friend, pulling the riffs back to earth when they float too far. Listeners get the pair's usual blend: half comedy set, half late-night philosophy session, with no script in sight.
uslaw-usc-t2-s1881c: Section 1881c of Title 2 of the United States Code allows funds for the Capitol flown flags plan for families of fallen heroes. Such sums as are needed may be granted for each fiscal year from 2017 through 2028. The money comes from sums granted each year for running the office of the Architect of the Capitol. One cap binds the whole span: the total for the plan across all those years may not top 40,000 dollars.
uslaw-usc-t2-s661c:
Section 661c of Title 2 of the United States Code covers budget treatment of federal credit programs. Title 2 covers Congress, and this section sits in the credit reform subchapter on budget and fiscal operations. The hosted text is the version current in twenty twenty six. Credit reform changed how loans are counted in the budget.

Beginning with fiscal year nineteen ninety two, the President's budget must reflect the costs of direct loan and loan guarantee programs. The budget must also include the planned level of new loan duties or guarantee pledges. Those pledges are tied to the programs the budget proposes. The rule forces the true cost of federal lending to show up front.
